**Learning Path**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |

| 4 | EDX1528 | Ordinary Differential Equations and Linear Algebra - Part 1 | edx | Continue with linear algebra, focusing on matrix algebra, solving systems of linear equations, and invertibility. |

**Path Explanation**

This learning path builds on prior knowledge, gradually increasing in cognitive load as the learner progresses. The path starts with a review of high school algebra, focusing on concepts such as functions, equations, and graphing. The learner then builds on this foundation, introducing new concepts such as linear, exponential, logarithmic, polynomial, rational, and trigonometric functions. The path continues with differential equations and linear algebra, focusing on qualitative analysis, separable equations, matrix algebra, and solving systems of linear equations. The learner then applies mathematical modeling and problem-solving, introducing new concepts such as function characteristics, properties, and rate of change of functions. Finally, the path focuses on engineering calculus, differential equations, and mathematical modeling, applying these concepts to real-world problems in kinematics, moments, and equilibrium.

| 3 | EDX1421 | High Conflict in Law: An Introduction | edx | Emphasis on critical thinking and analysis of high-conflict behaviors in law, introducing more complex concepts and ideas |
| 4 | EDX1764 | Genetic Models for Animal Breeding | edx | Practical application of genetic models and tools to predict breeding value, introducing a new area of law and its practical application |
| 5 | EDX2340 | Evaluating Animal Breeding Programmes | edx | Building on prior knowledge and skills, evaluating breeding programmes and genetic diversity, with a focus on practical application |
| 6 | EDX2853 | Basic Japanese Civil Law | edx | Introduction to a new area of law, basic Japanese civil law, with a focus on structure, justice system, and contemporary problems |
| 7 | EDX3100 | Introduction to American Civics: Presented by Zero-L | edx | Understanding of the design of the U.S. government and the distinctive roles of the Legislative, Executive, and Judicial Branches |
| 8 | EDX3225 | Business Sustainability Management | edx | Practical sustainability action plan to overcome barriers and aid in seizing opportunities associated with creating a sustainable business |
| 9 | EDX3242 | Negotiation Strategies | edx | Collaborative negotiation techniques and question-asking tools to understand the needs of your negotiation partner and maximize value for both parties |
| 10 | EDX3276 | Commercial and Contract Law | edx | Ability to read, interpret, and draft contracts within the South African business landscape, with a focus on practical application |
| 11 | EDX3303 | Negotiation and Conflict Resolution | edx | Ability to identify the causes of workplace conflict and recommend sustainable solutions, with a focus on practical application |
| 12 | EDX3364 | Paralegal Practitioner | edx | Wide-ranging knowledge of South African law and legal procedures, with a focus on practical application and skills development |

The learning path is designed to provide a comprehensive introduction to law and legal reasoning for a non-lawyer, progressing from foundational to advanced concepts. The path starts with a clear and concise introduction to the basics of law, including the structure of legal systems, key concepts, and fundamental principles. It then builds on this understanding, introducing more complex concepts and ideas, such as international law, high conflict in law, and negotiation strategies. The path also covers practical application of legal concepts, including evaluating animal breeding programmes, basic Japanese civil law, and commercial and contract law. Finally, the path concludes with a focus on practical application and skills development, including negotiation and conflict resolution, and paralegal practice.

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | EDX1247 | Beginners Guide to Cybersecurity | edx | Foundational course covering essential cybersecurity concepts, including data security, authentication, and threat analysis. |
| 2 | EDX1621 | Cybersecurity Fundamentals | edx | Builds on the previous course, introducing network and system administration fundamentals, as well as information assurance principles. |
| 3 | EDX904 | Try It: Ethical Hacking | edx | Introduces the basics of ethical hacking, including differences between ethical and unethical hackers, and common vulnerabilities associated with web applications. |
| 4 | EDX1781 | Ethical Hacking Essentials (EHE) | edx | Expands on the previous course, covering key issues plaguing the information security world, fundamentals of ethical hacking, and information security threats and vulnerabilities. |
| 5 | EDX996 | Cybersecurity Basics | edx | Covers the basics of cybersecurity, including penetration testing, cryptography, and firewalls, as well as social engineering and phishing attacks. |
| 6 | EDX3136 | Network Security - Protocols | edx | Introduces network security protocols, including substitution ciphers, cryptanalysis, and public key encryption. |
| 7 | EDX1789 | Introduction to Computer Science and Programming Using Python | edx | Transitions from cybersecurity to computer science, introducing the basics of programming with Python, including functions, variables, conditionals, and loops. |
| 8 | EDX1302 | Introduction to Deep Learning | edx | Introduces deep learning concepts, including justifying the development of state-of-the-art deep learning algorithms and implementing, optimizing, and tuning deep neural network architectures. |
| 9 | EDX665 | Shell Programming - A necessity for all Programmers | edx | Covers shell programming, including writing shell scripts, handling text, files, and directories, and using networking interfaces to communicate between programs. |
| 10 | EDX2911 | Preparing for the AP* Computer Science A Exam — Part 1 | edx | Prepares the learner for the AP* Computer Science A exam, covering topics such as variables, conditionals, objects, and primitives, as well as control structures and exceptions. |
| 11 | EDX1334 | Mathematical and Computational Methods | edx | Introduces mathematical and computational methods, including calculus, graph theory, and data structures, as well as algorithms and programming concepts. |
| 12 | EDX1060 | Secure Software Development: Implementation | edx | Covers secure software development, including implementation, input validation, process data securely, and handling problems such as error-handling code. |
| 13 | EDX3425 | Data Science with Python | edx | Introduces data science with Python, including applying data science and analysis techniques to inform decision-making, building and modifying robust models, and using Jupyter Notebook. |
| 14 | EDX2154 | Cloud Computing Security | edx | Covers cloud computing security, including evaluating security issues with cloud infrastructure, implementing cloud features to secure and harden the infrastructure, and using tools to analyze system logs. |
| 15 | EDX1712 | Essential Google Cloud Infrastructure: Core Services | edx | Introduces essential Google Cloud infrastructure, including administering Identity and Access Management for resources, implementing data storage services, and monitoring resources using Google Cloud's operations suite. |

The learning path is designed to progress from foundational courses in cybersecurity and computer science to more advanced topics in network security, deep learning, and cloud computing. Each course builds on the previous one, introducing new concepts and skills that the learner can apply to real-world scenarios. The path covers a range of topics, from threat analysis and vulnerability assessment to penetration testing and incident response, and includes hands-on exercises, simulations, and real-world projects to help the learner develop practical skills and a deeper understanding of cybersecurity and network defense concepts.

| 5 | COU1426 | How Do We Manage Climate Change? | Coursera | Understanding the strategies for mitigating and adapting to climate change |
| 6 | COU3894 | Science and Engineering of Climate Change | Coursera | Diving into the scientific and engineering aspects of climate change |
| 7 | COU795 | Paths to a Sustainable Future | Coursera | Exploring the pathways to a sustainable future, including climate action and sustainability |
| 8 | COU1423 | Renewable Energy Specialization | Coursera | Specializing in renewable energy, its technologies, and its applications |
| 9 | COU1174 | Hydro, Wind & Solar power: Resources, Variability & Forecast | Coursera | Advanced course on renewable energy, focusing on hydro, wind, and solar power |
| 10 | COU4464 | Act on Climate: Steps to Individual, Community, and Political Action | Coursera | Taking action on climate change, exploring individual, community, and political responses |

The final courses specialize in renewable energy and take action on climate change, exploring individual, community, and political responses.

| 4 | EDX2871 | CS50's Web Programming with Python and JavaScript | edX | Introduces Python and JavaScript programming, with a focus on web development and full-stack concepts. |
| 5 | COU548 | Learn JavaScript | Coursera | Delves deeper into JavaScript programming, covering advanced topics and best practices. |
| 6 | EDX1533 | Software Development Capstone Project | edX | Applies full-stack development concepts to a real-world project, using Python and JavaScript. |
| 7 | COU4442 | Frontend Development Specialization | Coursera | Focuses on frontend development, covering HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in-depth. |
| 8 | EDX2309 | Back-end Application Development with Node.js and Express | edX | Introduces back-end development with Node.js and Express, building on previous courses. |
| 9 | COU6214 | IBM Full-Stack JavaScript Developer Professional Certificate | Coursera | Covers full-stack development with JavaScript, including Node.js and Express. |
| 10 | EDX170 | Git and GitHub Basics | edX | Introduces version control and collaboration with Git and GitHub, essential for web development. |

**Path Explanation**

This learning path is designed to take the learner from foundational web development concepts to advanced full-stack development skills. The first period covers the basics of web development with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The second period builds on this foundation, introducing full-stack development concepts and the Django framework. The third period focuses on web design and development, with an emphasis on coding for non-technical professionals. The fourth period introduces Python and JavaScript programming, with a focus on web development and full-stack concepts. The fifth period delves deeper into JavaScript programming, covering advanced topics and best practices. The sixth period applies full-stack development concepts to a real-world project, using Python and JavaScript. The seventh period focuses on frontend development, covering HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in-depth. The eighth period introduces back-end development with Node.js and Express, building on previous courses. The ninth period covers full-stack development with JavaScript, including Node.js and Express. The final period introduces version control and collaboration with Git and GitHub, essential for web development.

This learning path starts with a foundational understanding of project management life cycle (EDX2192) and builds on existing knowledge with project management foundations (EDX3229). The path then introduces Agile project management principles and practices (EDX3248) and gradually increases in complexity with advanced project management concepts (EDX3326). The emphasis is on strategic thinking and decision-making (EDX3342), followed by practical application of project delivery methods and contracts (EDX1489). The path continues to build on existing knowledge, introducing project delivery methods and contracts, and emphasizes risk management and contract management. Finally, the path integrates Agile delivery principles and practices, and provides opportunities for practical application and hands-on experience.

| 3 | COU2929 | Genomics: Decoding the Universal Language of Life | Coursera | Introduction to genomics and genetics |
| 4 | COU5783 | Genomic Data Science Specialization | Coursera | Emphasis on concepts over memorization in genomics and data science |
| 5 | COU1249 | Finding Mutations in DNA and Proteins (Bioinformatics VI) | Coursera | Gradual complexity in bioinformatics and genomics |
| 6 | COU5134 | Python for Genomic Data Science | Coursera | Integration of visual and interactive learning in Python programming |
| 7 | COU3367 | Contemporary Biology | Coursera | Building on prior knowledge in biology and genetics |
| 8 | COU3709 | Introduction to Genetics and Evolution | Coursera | Emphasis on concepts over memorization in genetics and evolution |
| 9 | COU318 | Comparing Genes, Proteins, and Genomes (Bioinformatics III) | Coursera | Gradual complexity in bioinformatics and genomics |
| 10 | COU3697 | Industrial Biotechnology | Coursera | Introduction to industrial biotechnology and its applications |

**How the path fits together**

This learning path starts with a foundational course in biology and programming (COU149), followed by a course that builds on prior knowledge in biology and genetics (COU2930). The next course introduces genomics and genetics (COU2929), and then delves into genomics and data science (COU5783). The path continues with a course on finding mutations in DNA and proteins (COU1249), which emphasizes concepts over memorization in bioinformatics and genomics. The next course focuses on Python programming for genomic data science (COU5134), incorporating visual and interactive learning. The path then builds on prior knowledge in biology and genetics (COU3367), followed by a course on genetics and evolution (COU3709). The final courses in the path cover bioinformatics and genomics (COU318) and industrial biotechnology (COU3697). This learning path provides a comprehensive and structured approach to molecular biology and genetics, with a focus on building on prior knowledge and skills.

| 5 | EDX861 | Circuits and Electronics 2: Amplification, Speed, and Delay | edx | Focuses on amplifier design and the analysis of circuit behavior, including time and frequency behavior. |

| 7 | EDX848 | Introduction to the Internet of Things | edx | Covers the basics of electronics for programming microcontrollers and sensors, as well as data analysis and display. |
| 8 | EDX1130 | RF Design: Passive and Active Components | edx | Develops the learner's understanding of RF design, including passive and active components, and CAD tools. |
| 9 | EDX361 | Electromagnetic Compatibility Essentials | edx | Introduces the principles of electromagnetic compatibility, including noise suppression and electrostatic discharge. |
| 10 | EDX2308 | Semiconductors for Beginners | edx | Covers the basics of semiconductors, including static electricity, ionization, and material properties. |
| 11 | EDX1475 | Primer on RF Design | edx | Provides a primer on RF design, including system and module design principles. |
| 12 | EDX2480 | Introduction to Semiconductors, PN Junctions and Bipolar Junction Transistors | edx | Introduces the operational principles of semiconductors, PN junctions, and bipolar junction transistors. |
| 13 | EDX2320 | Fundamentals of Transistors | edx | Develops the learner's understanding of transistor fundamentals, including IV characteristics and device metrics. |
| 14 | EDX917 | Nanotechnology: Fundamentals of Nanotransistors | edx | Covers the basics of nanotechnology and nanotransistors, including transistor fundamentals and MOS electrostatics. |
| 15 | EDX3038 | Designing Electronics for Recycling in a Circular Economy | edx | Introduces the principles of designing electronics for recycling, including value creation and value recovery. |
